lede: You cannot see photosynthesis happening, so you test for the starch it leaves behind. Destarch the plant first, take away one thing — light, carbon dioxide or chlorophyll — and the pattern of blue-black on the leaf afterwards tells you what the plant needed.
can: Describe destarching and give a reason for each step of the starch test.
Set up the tests for light, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll.
Write a conclusion that names both halves of the comparison.

md: Boil a leaf, take the green out with ethanol and drop iodine on it: where the leaf made starch it turns blue-black. That one colour change is how you prove a plant needs light, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll. Every step in the method has a reason.

prompt: A leaf that contains starch turns ______ when iodine solution is added.
explain: Blue-black. If there is no starch it stays the yellow-brown colour the iodine already was.

md:
**Why each step happens.**
**1 Boil in water** — kills the leaf, stops its reactions and breaks the cells open so the next liquids can get in.
**2 Boil in ethanol, in a water bath** — the chlorophyll dissolves out, so the green colour cannot hide the result. Ethanol catches fire easily, so **the Bunsen is turned off** and the tube stands in hot water.
**3 Dip in hot water** — the ethanol leaves the leaf brittle; the water softens it so it can be spread flat.
**4 Iodine solution on a white tile** — the white background is what lets you see the blue-black.

prompt: Why is the Bunsen turned off before the leaf goes into the ethanol?
options: ethanol would turn the leaf blue
explain: Ethanol is flammable, so it is heated in a water bath with the flame out.

title: Summer 2024 Unit 7 Biology Booklet B Q2
md: The safety mark was for **switching off the Bunsen burner** before the ethanol was heated. Examiners reported that many candidates gave a general rule — tie your hair back, wear goggles — and got nothing, because the precaution has to match the hazard in front of it. Ethanol is flammable, so the answer is about the flame.

prompt: Why is the leaf boiled in ethanol?
options: To remove the chlorophyll so the colour change can be seen
answer: To remove the chlorophyll so the colour change can be seen
explain: Killing is step 1 and softening is step 3. Ethanol is there to take the green out.

md: **Destarching comes first.** Leave the plant in the **dark for 48 hours**. The leaves use up the starch they already had, so any starch you find afterwards must have been made during the investigation. Skip this and the result proves nothing — every leaf would go blue-black whatever you did to it.

prompt: To destarch a plant you leave it in the dark for about how many hours?
explain: Forty-eight hours — two days. The mark for 'why' is that the starch already in the leaves is used up.

md:
**Light** — clip black card over part of one leaf and leave the plant in the light for 48 hours. The covered strip stays yellow-brown, the rest goes blue-black.
**Carbon dioxide** — seal a leaf in a flask standing over **sodium hydroxide solution**, which absorbs the carbon dioxide. That leaf stays yellow-brown even in full light.
**Chlorophyll** — use a **variegated** leaf, one with green and white parts. Only the green parts go blue-black.

alt: A potted geranium with variegated leaves: each leaf has a dark green centre and a broad cream-white band round its edge
credit: Forest and Kim Starr, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
caption: A variegated geranium: dark green in the middle, cream-white round the edge.
prompt: This leaf is destarched, left in bright light for 48 hours and tested for starch. Sketch which parts go blue-black, and say what that shows.
A destarched variegated leaf is left in bright light and tested for starch. Which parts turn blue-black?
explain: The white parts have no chlorophyll, so they cannot absorb light energy and make no starch. That is the whole point of using a variegated leaf.

title: Why a variegated leaf beats two separate plants
md: Two plants would differ in more than their chlorophyll — age, water, how much light each one caught. On one variegated leaf the green and white parts share the same temperature, the same light, the same water and the same carbon dioxide. **Only the chlorophyll is different**, so only the chlorophyll can explain the difference in result. That is what makes the investigation valid.

alt: Three slices of apple on a bench after iodine solution has been added: the first has stained blue-black only in a ring near the skin, the second is blue-black over most of its area with a pale centre, and the third is blue-black almost all over
caption: Iodine solution on cut slices: where there is starch the tissue stains blue-black; where there is little or none it stays pale.
prompt: One slice is blue-black only near its edge. What does the pale centre tell you, and what would you have to do before you could say the same about a leaf?

md: **Oxygen is the other half of the equation.** Pondweed in water under a lamp gives off bubbles; collect them in an inverted test tube and test the gas with a **glowing splint**. If the splint **relights**, the gas is oxygen. Counting the bubbles per minute is how the same apparatus turns into a rate investigation.

prompt: How do you show the gas collected from pondweed is oxygen?
options: A lit splint gives a squeaky pop
explain: The squeaky pop is hydrogen and milky limewater is carbon dioxide. Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

md: A conclusion is only as good as its comparison. 'The covered part had no starch' proves nothing by itself; **'the covered part had no starch while the uncovered part of the same leaf did'** proves that light is needed. Write both halves. The same rule applies to the flask and to the variegated leaf.

prompt: Which sentence would earn the conclusion mark?
options: The covered part stayed yellow-brown but the uncovered part of the same leaf went blue-black, so light is needed
The leaf went blue-black, so photosynthesis happened
There was no starch in the leaf because there was no light
answer: The covered part stayed yellow-brown but the uncovered part of the same leaf went blue-black, so light is needed
explain: It names both parts, both colours and the conclusion. The other two either leave out the comparison or restate the question.
